title: Drag to move the view port
idea: Holding Shift and left dragging moves the view port, whether or not an npc is selected (issue 7).

glossary.meaning: The part of the map shown in the window; the existing camera.
Pressing the left mouse button with Shift held and moving the mouse until the button is released.

features.name: View drag
features.whatItDoes: Moves the view port with Shift + left drag.
details: It works whether or not npcs are selected, and the selection does not change.
The map point under the cursor at the press stays under the cursor during the drag.
The view port stops at the map's edge, like every other camera move.
Moving the cursor to the window's edge no longer moves the camera, during a drag or at any other time.

features.name: Zoom steps
features.whatItDoes: Makes each wheel notch change the zoom by a smaller amount.
details: One notch moves zoom by 0.25 instead of 1.
The lowest and highest zoom stay the same, and the map point under the cursor stays under it.

features.name: Mouse cursor
features.whatItDoes: Shows pixel-art cursors from assets/ui/cursor instead of the system cursor.
details: grab-close shows during a view drag.
point shows during a box select, and over an npc that is on screen and not hidden by the veil, except during a view drag.

flows.name: Look around while keeping a selection
steps: Hold Shift, press the left button on the map and move the mouse; the map follows the cursor.
Release the left button; the view port stays where it is and the selection is unchanged.

examples.situation: Two npcs are selected and the player Shift + left drags to the left.
examples.whatHappens: The map moves left with the cursor, and both npcs stay selected.

examples.situation: A view drag reaches the map's edge.
examples.whatHappens: The view port stops at the edge while the cursor keeps moving.

examples.situation: The cursor rests at the window's edge.

leftOut: A separate drag mode toggled by a key.

decisions.decision: The view port moves with Shift + left drag, with or without a selection; there is no drag mode.
decisions.reason: The user first asked for a G toggle, then replaced it with Shift + left click.

decisions.decision: The map point grabbed stays under the cursor.
Edge scroll stays in the game but is off during a view drag.
decisions.reason: The user chose to turn edge scroll off only while dragging.

decisions.decision: project.spec.json is the view drag spec; the finished fog of war spec moved to docs/specs/fog-of-war.spec.json.
Replaces D-3: edge scroll is removed from the game; the camera moves only by a view drag and zoom.
decisions.reason: The user asked to take it out.

decisions.decision: Zoom uses smaller steps, so it can be fractional instead of a whole number of screen pixels per map px.
decisions.reason: The user said zooming was too fast.

decisions.decision: The cursor is grab-open by default, grab-close on Shift + left, and point over an npc or during a box select.

assumptions.statement: Shift only matters at the press: releasing it during a view drag does not end the drag, and pressing it during a box select does not start one.
A Shift + left press does not select anything, even if the mouse does not move.
A plain left click and left drag still select, and Shift + right click still queues a destination.
While placing walls, a left drag plans walls even with Shift held.
A Shift + left press on the Terminal button still opens the Terminal.
The user shrank the cursor and asked for the nearest whole scale: each cursor art px draws as 1 point, so a 16 px cursor is 16 points.
Any visible npc shows point, including enemies.
A smaller zoom step means 0.25 per wheel notch.
Over the open Terminal the cursor is left to the Terminal, so its resize cursors keep working.
